messages:
Ben: Hey team — running into SSL failures when the Python SDK talks to our Dedicated endpoint behind corp proxy + custom CA. Root error: certificate verify failed / tlsv1 alert unknown ca. Happening with both sync and async flows.

Ben: Minimal repro (async):
```python
# using redwood-python v0.x (httpx under the hood)
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient

os.environ['REDWOOD_BASE_URL'] = 'https://dedicated.internal.corp'
os.environ['SSL_CERT_FILE'] = '/etc/ssl/certs/corp-chain.pem'

client = RedwoodClient(api_key='s.xxxx', base_url=os.environ['REDWOOD_BASE_URL'])
await client.chat.create(model='x', input='hi')
# -> ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] unable to get local issuer certificate
```

Ben: I also tried setting REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and SSL_CERT_FILE and passing verify='/etc/ssl/certs/corp-chain.pem' to the underlying requests session via monkeypatching, but the async path still fails.

Alice: Hmm. httpx AsyncClient doesn't always pick up REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE unless trust_env is True and proxies/env vars are present. Also on some Linux images the cert bundle path expected by certifi vs SSL_CERT_FILE differ. Which SDK version are you on?

Ben: v0.9.2. I think the SDK wraps httpx.AsyncClient without exposing verify/ssl_context/trust_env options in the typed constructor for the high-level client (and our wrappers don't forward proxies).

Carol: Two things I've seen before in corp setups: (1) the proxy does TLS interception and adds its own cert, so the client needs the full chain in the truststore; (2) SNI/Host rewrites can cause the server cert to be presented for a different name. If the proxy rewrites the Host header or terminates TLS, you can see mismatched SNI errors. Any error text about "certificate common name" or "hostname mismatch"?

Ben: No hostname mismatch text, just unknown ca. The proxy is a corporate forward proxy (CONNECT) that doesn't rewrite SNI, but our Dedicated frontends are behind an edge that expects SNI="models.redwood.internal". The customer's internal CA signs the proxy leaf cert.

Infra-bot: Noted: Dedicated private endpoints expose a TLS name that includes the customer subdomain. If your proxy inserts a custom cert chain, you need to 1) trust the corporate CA bundle and 2) ensure client SNI is preserved. Some versions of httpx/urllib3 set server_hostname based on the URL host; if your base_url uses the internal loadbalancer name but the proxy does Host rewrites, that can break.

Alice: Workarounds you can try locally: set SSL_CERT_FILE to the bundle path AND set env var HTTPX_DISABLE_CERTIFI=1 (if present in your environment) or point certifi.where() to your bundle. Also try constructing an ssl.SSLContext and pass into httpx via transport, e.g.:
```python
import ssl, httpx
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/ssl/certs/corp-chain.pem')
transport = httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(ssl_context=ctx, keepalive_expiry=5.0)
client = httpx.AsyncClient(transport=transport, trust_env=True)
```
Then pass that transport to the SDK if possible.

Ben: That's the problem — our RedwoodClient doesn't accept a transport, ssl_context, or verify kwarg in the public typed signature. I had to monkeypatch internals to inject the transport and it worked. But that's awful for customers.

Sam: Filing a feature request: SDK should accept verify / ssl_context / transport and trust_env / proxies options (and document them) on both sync and async clients. Also type stubs need to include these params so static typing catches it.

Carol: Agreed. Also request: allow base_url to accept an optional "sni_host" arg so the client can set server_hostname independent of the URL (useful for when internal hostnames differ). Might be contentious but small/explicit opt-in could help.

Ben: For immediate triage I opened GH issue #4321 with repro steps and the monkeypatch workaround. Can someone from devex/infra review and decide whether to accept ssl_context/verify in the next patch release? Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/issues/4321

Infra-bot: Issue #4321 created and labelled devex, p1 for Dedicated onboarding. Assigning to Alice.

Alice: I'll put together a short PR that exposes a low-level AsyncClient kwargs passthrough and add typed overloads. Two notes: we should avoid encouraging insecure skip_verify, so default verify behavior should remain strict; add clear docs showing how to supply a custom CA bundle and how to use trust_env for proxies.

Ben: Thanks. Also could we add a short section in the Dedicated onboarding guide about env var precedence: SSL_CERT_FILE vs REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE vs REDWOOD_TRUST_BUNDLE (our proposed env var) and examples for Windows, macOS, Linux? That would save us from these Slack threads. :pray:

Sam: I'll add a ticket to docs to write that onboarding paragraph and a checklist for electron/desktop customers (they often ship their own cert bundle).

Carol: For the prod-side fix: infra should also confirm the edge doesn't unintentionally rewrite SNI or Host for Dedicated private endpoints. If it does, we need to accept an explicit Host override at the edge.

Ben: Great. I'll paste the monkeypatch snippet I used into the GH issue as a temporary workaround.

Ben: Monkeypatch snippet: 
```python
# minimal hack to inject ssl_context into SDK internals
import ssl, httpx
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/ssl/certs/corp-chain.pem')
transport = httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(ssl_context=ctx, trust_env=True)
# internal: redwood._transport = transport  # ugly but works until SDK exposes transport param
```

Alice: Thanks Ben. I'll follow up in the issue with a concrete PR plan and a typed signature proposal for both RedwoodClient and AsyncRedwoodClient.

Ben: Awesome. Leaving the thread here; I'll post updates in the GH issue.
